tagline.hi: वेबसाइटों को साफ़, LLM-तैयार Markdown में बदलता है, API और प्लेग्राउंड के साथ

notes: Every API call needs the token from the first-run card, sent as the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. Without it, or with a wrong one, Crawl4AI answers 401. Only /health, / and the static pages of the playground and dashboard are public, and they hold no data. The token is upstream's own CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN, so there is no extra password gate.

The playground at /playground/ (the site's address redirects there) has an API token box at the top: paste the token and click Set, and the playground sends it with every request. It is kept only for that browser tab.

Example: curl -X POST https://<your domain>/crawl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"urls":["https://example.com"]}' returns the page as Markdown in results[0].markdown.raw_markdown (results[0].markdown also holds fit_markdown and markdown_with_citations); POST /md with {"url": "https://example.com"} returns it directly as markdown.

Crawl4AI runs a headless Chromium pool inside the container. The panel writes upstream's config.yml for 0.9.5 to the site directory once (app/config.yml, mounted read-only on /app/config.yml) with the pool made smaller so it fits the 2 GB memory floor: at most 10 pages open at the same time (upstream 40), no new browser above 85% of the container's memory limit (upstream 95%) and 2 background job workers (upstream 4). Raise them together with the memory limit if you need more parallel crawls. Edit the file in the File Manager and restart the app; the panel never overwrites it.

shm_size is 1gb as upstream's compose file sets it. Upstream's compose also drops every Linux capability, and so does this one. Upstream's read-only root filesystem and tmpfs mounts are left out: nothing in the container keeps state, so there is no data volume, and a re-create starts clean (finished job results in its internal Redis are lost, which upstream's one-hour task TTL does anyway).

FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=* makes the image's gunicorn/uvicorn honour the panel proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto. Without it uvicorn trusts only 127.0.0.1, but the proxy reaches the container from the Docker network gateway, so the playground's trailing-slash redirect (/playground to /playground/) pointed at http:// and a token pasted there went over plain HTTP (found live, RC-48). The port is published on 127.0.0.1 only, so the panel proxy is the only client that can set these headers.

Upstream's safe defaults stay on: deep crawling over the API, hooks and the execute_js endpoint are off, and crawling private and loopback addresses is refused. LLM features (/md with an LLM filter, /llm, LLM extraction) need a provider key: add for example OPENAI_API_KEY and LLM_PROVIDER to the environment in the panel.

SECRET_KEY, which would sign JWTs, is generated by the panel so upstream does not start with an ephemeral one. Upstream's /token endpoint stays disabled, because it only issues JWTs when an api_token is written in config.yml; use the static token instead.
The image is about 2.3 GB to download (8.2 GB unpacked on disk, which stays after the app is deleted until unused images are pruned), so the first install takes 3 to 4 minutes.

Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-48, Medium boxes: 2 vCPU, 4 GB): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running in 179 s (26.04) and 251 s (24.04), most of it the image pull. Without the token, or with a wrong one, /crawl, /md and /schema answered 401 and /health 200; with it, /crawl and /md on https://example.com returned the page (title Example Domain) as Markdown, in 2.4 to 2.8 s with a cold browser and under 0.5 s warm; crawling 127.0.0.1, localhost and 169.254.169.254 was refused with 400; 4 parallel crawls (example.com, Wikipedia, docs.crawl4ai.com, python.org) all succeeded. The playground answered 401 without the token and crawled after Set. A restart and a forced re-create worked again in 11 to 23 s with the same token and config. Memory: 450 to 480 MiB idle after start, 745 to 926 MiB with the browser pool warm, peak 897 to 952 MiB (under half of 2g) during the 4 parallel crawls; never restarted or OOM-killed. The first run found the playground redirect falling back to http://; after the FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS fix both boxes were upgraded, the app re-created, and /, /playground and /dashboard stayed on https:// in curl and in Chromium, with the token checks unchanged. Every image ref above is in its tested list.
